chunks: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid (may Allah have mercy on him) narrated to us. He said: Al-Husayn ibn al-Hasan ibn Aban narrated to us from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from al-Qasim ibn Muhammad from Ishaq ibn Harun from Harun ibn Hamza al-Ghanawi. He said:

I heard al-Sadiq Ja'far ibn Muhammad (peace be upon him) say: Allah the Blessed and Exalted designated four thousand angels at the grave of al-Husayn (peace be upon him) -- disheveled and dusty -- weeping for him until the Day of Resurrection. Whoever visits him, recognizing his right, they will be party to him until he reaches his home; if he becomes ill, they will visit him morning and evening; and if he dies, they will attend his funeral and seek forgiveness for him until the Day of Resurrection.

key_terms.زيارة: Visitation -- the act of visiting the grave of Imam al-Husayn as a devotional practice
key_terms.شعثا غبرا: Disheveled and dusty -- a description of deep mourning among the angels
key_terms.مأمن: Place of safety, sanctuary -- the visitor's safe return home

ai.seo_question: What did Imam al-Sadiq say about the four thousand angels at the grave of Imam al-Husayn?
ai.summary: Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (AS) reports that Allah has appointed four thousand angels to weep at the grave of Imam al-Husayn (AS) until the Day of Resurrection. These angels, described as disheveled and dusty in mourning, serve as spiritual companions to those who visit the grave recognizing his right: they escort the visitor home safely, visit him if he falls ill, attend his funeral if he dies, and seek forgiveness for him until the Day of Resurrection. This hadith establishes the theological significance of Husayn's martyrdom at Karbala and the rewards of his visitation (ziyara).
